facts.claim: Ramp offers a financial operations platform covering corporate cards, expenses, bill payments, procurement, vendor management, travel, banking, and accounting automation.

facts.excerpt: Ramp supports more than $100 billion in annualized card and AP payment volume, and customers save 5% or more on average with Ramp.

research.website_note: The results identify ramp.com as Ramp’s official website and name Ramp Business Corporation in its site disclosures.

strategy.observation: Ramp said it released more than 70 products and major features in the preceding few months and planned to begin serving companies headquartered in the UK and Europe that summer.
strategy.offer_link: A set of expense policy templates could give Ramp’s content team a practical resource for finance teams alongside its expanding product and market coverage.
hypotheses: Ramp may want more practical, downloadable content to help finance teams understand or implement expense policies.
The templates may need adaptation for UK and European audiences to be useful alongside Ramp’s planned market expansion.
strategy.angle: With Ramp releasing more than 70 products and major features recently and preparing to serve UK and European companies, expense policy templates could be a practical resource for finance teams exploring its expense tools.
strategy.fit_reason: Templates could plausibly support Ramp’s content marketing, but the facts do not show that the content team is seeking this kind of asset, and the offer is scoped to mid-size teams rather than Ramp’s broader market.

draft.subject: Expense policy templates
draft.body:
I create expense policy templates for mid-size finance teams. They could give Ramp’s content team a practical resource alongside its expanding expense tools.

Ramp said it released more than 70 products and major features in recent months and planned to begin serving companies headquartered in the UK and Europe that summer. If templates tailored to those companies fit your content plans, would you be open to reviewing a one-page outline?

draft.subject: Expense policy templates for Ramp
draft.body:
Ramp said it had released more than 70 products and major features recently, with UK and European expansion planned for that summer. Practical policy guidance could help finance teams put expense tools into context as Ramp enters those markets.

I create expense policy templates for mid-size finance teams. Would UK- and Europe-specific templates be relevant to the content you’re planning around that expansion?

issues: “as Ramp enters those markets” implies Ramp has entered the UK and European markets, but the supplied fact only says it planned to begin serving companies headquartered there that summer. Change this to “as Ramp plans to enter those markets.”

issues: “planned to begin serving companies headquartered in the UK and Europe that summer” — This is supported, but “as Ramp plans to enter those markets” broadens the claim beyond serving companies headquartered there. Keep the narrower wording about serving those companies.

“Ramp said it had released more than 70 products and major features in recent months” — The email leads with background rather than the offer, so the point does not appear in the first line. Lead with the expense policy template offer.
